C1.label: ASSUMED
C1.text: Observation, not a sealed claim: the canon docstring of MRAB.mrab_bound_le_baseRate (MRAB.lean, sha256 f56396bf...54db2e7) says adding rings can only shrink the joint budget, but the theorem compares mrabBound with baseRate at the same K. With P = kB = T = 1, one ring D = (1/4), c = (1) gives ceiling (1/4)/ln 2, while adding a perfectly aligned ring D = (1/4, 1), c = (1, 1) gives (1/2)/ln 2; this inequality is an elaborated example in proposals/P2.MultiRingAlignment.lean.

C2.label: ASSUMED
C2.text: Observation, not a sealed claim: in the canon Intelligence Bound definitions, mutual information is Mathlib's klDiv (natural log), so rates are in nats while the Landauer factor kB*T*ln 2 is per bit; SatisfiesLandauerLimit is thus weaker by a factor ln 2 than the per-nat Landauer inequality. Also, entropy defined as self-information I(V;V) is infinite for a real variable with an atomless law (argued, not formalised).
